Variants.Content: The Shivering Sea stretches between northern Westeros and the northern shores of Essos, affecting Eastwatch, Skagos, Ibben, and the Cold Sea routes beyond. The sea water is cold, foggy, gusty winds and ice floes can damage ship decks and masts, and the sailing window is especially short in winter. Fish, seals, cetaceans, furs, and timber attracted ships to adventure, while hypothermia, bad water, and the inability to reach shore were more common killers than pirates. Northern sailors would strengthen their bows, store grease and thick clothing, and also rely on local piloting knowledge to judge ice lines. The Shivering Sea connects the settlements on the edge of the map, but requires paying a price for the cold first for every exchange.

When people on the east coast look at the Shivering Sea, they first look at the ice and fog. When a southern captain asks how many days the voyage will take, the locals will ask how thick the hull is and whether they have enough oil and spare oars.

The Iban whalers regarded the Cold Sea as their home, and would never call it docile. Behind every barrel of whale oil is the shadow of a ship that has been waiting for a long time and may not return.
Foreign rulers see routes from charts, scholars see climate from reports, and travelers see endless grayness from decks. Only the last perspective will truly make sense of distance.
